channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Jizzakh Region Explores New Projects with Chinese Investors
item.description: Jizzakh region officials met with a Chinese delegation to discuss expanding partnerships with the China Center for International Cultural Communication and JDB Group. Priority projects include a modern hotel complex, a traditional Chinese medicine wellness center, and a sanatorium in the mountainous area. A vocational training center and agricultural processing logistics center are also planned.

item.title: 6.4 km of Asphalt Laid on Tayan-Zardaly Road in Batken Region
item.description: The Tayan-Zardaly road in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region has been asphalted for 6.4 km, with protective barriers being installed on dangerous sections. The road, leading to the remote village of Zardaly, was previously widened to 10 meters. Further improvements to remaining sections are planned, following the completion of a 17.5 km road and bridge project in December 2025.

item.title: Air Astana Group Reports $2.7 Million Net Loss Despite Revenue Growth
item.description: Air Astana Group reported a net loss of $2.7 million for the first nine months of 2026, despite a 17.9% increase in revenue to $1.293 billion. Operating expenses rose faster than revenue, primarily due to a 22.4% increase in fuel costs. The group incurred a $21.2 million loss in the first half but a $18.5 million profit in the third quarter.

item.title: Samruk-Kazyna Assures Stability After Official's Detainment
item.description: The Samruk-Kazyna fund has issued a statement affirming its financial and institutional stability following the detention of an official. The fund emphasized that all obligations to investors, creditors, and partners remain valid and are being met. Investment projects and strategic programs continue to be implemented as planned.

item.title: Kazakh Company to Explore for Gold in Tajikistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Solidcore Resources has signed a memorandum with Tajikistan's geology department to jointly explore for precious metals and polymetallic ores over five years. The agreement aims to assess the country's geological potential, identify promising areas, and evaluate mineral reserves using modern technologies and international standards.

item.title: MBANK Joins UNICEF Business Advisory Council for Children's Rights
item.description: MBANK has joined the UNICEF Business Advisory Council for Children's Rights, with its Chairman and the UNICEF Representative in Kyrgyzstan signing the agreement. The council unites business leaders to promote children's rights and responsible business practices. MBANK will focus on financial literacy and digital security for children and families. The bank aims to enhance financial literacy nationwide through its ecosystem and MJunior app.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Meets Central Asia and China Construction Ministers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov met with construction ministers from Central Asian countries and China on November 12. Discussions focused on developing cooperation in the construction sector, the 'My Home' housing program, and preparations for the third summit of the 'Central Asia - China' format. Japarov highlighted the format's practical development and the importance of the treaty on eternal good-neighborliness. The third summit is planned for 2027 in China.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Junda Oil Refinery Faces Pollution Concerns Amid Upgrade
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Junda oil refinery is undergoing a $194 million upgrade, but residents near Kara-Balta have reported health issues they attribute to refinery pollution. President Japarov stated the government would consider relocating residents if their health is harmed. The refinery is installing a vapor recovery system and plans to plant trees.

item.title: Uzbekistan's dollar exchange rate increases, Central Bank announces November 13 rates
item.description: The exchange rate of the US dollar against the Uzbek soum has risen. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies valid on November 13.

item.title: Uzbekistan's COP31 Initiatives Reshape Regional Climate Agenda
item.description: Uzbekistan's President presented key proposals at COP31 in Antalya, addressing global environmental challenges like climate change, water scarcity, and land degradation. These initiatives aim to strengthen international environmental cooperation and influence the region's climate policy. The summit gathered leaders from over 90 countries.

item.title: Tajikistan's Emomali Rahmon and Russia's Vladimir Putin Discuss Security and Economy
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon met with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin in Moscow to discuss regional security, trade, economic cooperation, energy, digitalization, and labor migration. The leaders emphasized the high level of political dialogue and the need to implement previous agreements. They also explored cooperation in new technologies and humanitarian spheres.

item.title: UN OCHA: Drought and Water Shortages Pushing Afghanistan to the Brink
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warns that drought and water shortages in Afghanistan are pushing communities to the brink of collapse. Those least responsible for the climate crisis are suffering the most. OCHA stresses the need for accessible climate financing for affected populations.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Commission to Study School Meals and Energy Drink Sales to Minors
item.description: A temporary parliamentary commission in Kyrgyzstan has begun investigating the safety of energy drinks and the quality of food products, including organic options, for schools and kindergartens. The commission will assess compliance with safety standards, the effectiveness of state control, and legislative gaps. It aims to propose improvements to legislation and procurement mechanisms.

item.title: Tashkent building roof removed during rain causing flooding
item.description: In Tashkent, the demolition of an illegal structure on the roof of a 17-story building led to flooding of the upper floor during rainfall. The construction inspection confirmed the incident and stated that roof repairs are underway. The illegal addition was constructed by Alaniya Stroy Servis.

item.title: Samruk-Kazyna Fund Continues Operations Amidst Corruption Arrests
item.description: The Samruk-Kazyna Fund has issued a statement assuring that operations continue as usual following the detention of its head, Nurlan Zhakupov, on corruption charges. The fund confirmed that all commitments to investors, creditors, and partners remain valid and are being fulfilled according to agreements.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows AI Use in Diplomas with Strict Guidelines
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Science and Higher Education permits students to use artificial intelligence in diploma work, but with specific limitations. AI cannot be used for analysis, conclusions, or summaries, which must be student-authored. Proper citation of AI usage is mandatory. Universities will set internal rules on AI integration.

item.title: ADB Approves $60 Million Loan for Uzbekistan's Livestock Sector
item.description: The Asian Development Bank has approved a $60 million loan to boost livestock farming productivity in Uzbekistan, particularly in drought-prone regions. The project will support around 29,000 smallholder farmers, improve fodder production, restore watering points, and enhance veterinary services, incorporating AI for pasture monitoring.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Leads EAEU in Fuel and Electricity Price Increases
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has experienced the highest annual increases in consumer prices for gasoline, diesel, and electricity among Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) member states. In September, it also ranked second in the EAEU for the average price of a liter of gasoline and diesel in dollar terms. Producer prices also saw significant rises.

item.title: Taraz Court Overturns Decision to Remove Child's Disability Status
item.description: A court in Taraz has ruled illegal and overturned a decision to remove a child's disability status. The child, who has a congenital disorder, had their disability status reinstated after a review found the initial assessment incomplete, lacking input from a maxillofacial surgeon. The court emphasized considering social factors alongside medical indicators.

item.title: Samruk-Kazyna Head Nurlan Zhakupov's Income Revealed Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Nurlan Zhakupov, the arrested chairman of the Samruk-Kazyna national wealth fund, declared hundreds of millions of tenge in income over the past three years. His declared income shows a decrease from 422 million tenge in 2022 to 186 million in 2023 and 197 million in 2024. The fund is cooperating with authorities in the investigation.

item.title: Japan's JTI to Fund Expansion of Uzbekistan's Clean Water Project Through 2028
item.description: Japan's JTI company plans to extend funding for Uzbekistan's clean drinking water and sanitation project until 2027-2028. The project, initiated in 2023, aims to provide clean water to remote areas. It has already supplied water to thousands in Namangan and Fergana regions, with plans to reach more communities.

item.title: Kazakhstan-Linked Hackers Used AI to Steal Over 2,000 Tajik Defense Documents
item.description: Cybersecurity firm CloudSEK reports that hackers linked to Kazakhstan used an AI tool, Hermes Agent, to steal over 2,000 documents from Tajikistan's Defense Ministry. The stolen data includes flight requests and military personnel transfers. The group, Silent Lynx, gained access via a railway employee's account.

item.title: Samruk-Kazyna Assures Normal Operations Following Head's Detention Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Kazakhstan's sovereign wealth fund, Samruk-Kazyna, stated that its operations and all commitments to investors and partners remain unaffected following the detention of its chairman, Nurlan Zhakupov, for alleged corruption. The fund is cooperating with law enforcement in the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Election campaign to begin December 23, Central Election Commission states
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, presidential candidates can begin their election campaign on December 23, after official registration. The Central Election Commission will monitor compliance with campaign laws. Violations can be reported to the commission, which has working groups to review complaints and make decisions. The presidential election is scheduled for January 27, 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan sign memorandum to restore saiga population
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have signed a memorandum to conserve and restore the saiga population. The agreement includes protecting migration routes, joint monitoring, and combating poaching. Both countries will exchange scientific data and implement reintroduction programs in historical habitats. Efforts will focus on joint anti-poaching raids and developing transboundary protected areas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to expand network of toll roads, including Osh and Nookat bypasses
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to expand its network of toll roads, with new projects including bypasses around Osh and Nookat, and an alternative Bishkek-Belogorka-Suusamyr route. These projects will involve private investors, with costs recouped through tolls. The new Bishkek bypass and a Chon-Kurchak project are also planned. The Uzgen bypass serves as a current example of a toll road.

item.title: Kazakhstan to cease budget contributions for mothers on parental leave
item.description: Kazakhstan will stop making state budget contributions to pension funds for mothers on parental leave. This change affects payments made on behalf of women during their childcare leave. The government has decided to discontinue this practice, impacting future pension calculations for affected individuals.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Regional Disaster Warning System at COP31
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed establishing a joint early warning system for natural disasters in Central Asia, including greater climate data sharing and coordinated funding for land restoration. President Mirziyoyev presented the initiative at the COP31 summit, emphasizing the need for international cooperation to address climate change challenges.

item.title: UN-Habitat Stresses Need for Shelter for Returning Afghans
item.description: UN-Habitat has highlighted the urgent need for shelter for the over six million migrants who have returned to Afghanistan since 2023. The agency stated that returning families require safe housing, essential support, and protection, calling for increased cooperation and resources to meet their basic needs.

item.title: Bishkek TET Officials Urged to Enhance Equipment Control and Fuel Reserves
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Erlist Akunbekov, has ordered increased oversight of the Bishkek Thermal Power Plant's equipment and ensured sufficient fuel supplies for the upcoming winter. This directive follows a meeting assessing readiness for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter period. Akunbekov inspected the plant and discussed measures to prevent emergencies.

item.title: Lawyer Klara Sooronkulova Becomes 11th Candidate for Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: Lawyer and public figure Klara Sooronkulova has submitted her application to run for president of Kyrgyzstan, becoming the 11th contender for the January 27, 2027 election. A former judge and leader of the 'Reforma' party, Sooronkulova previously ran in the 2021 presidential election. She joins ten other candidates who have also filed their applications.

item.title: Bishkek Vice-Mayor: Traffic Congestion Could Reduce by 40% by 2030 with Measures
item.description: Bishkek's vice-mayor, Ramiz Aliyev, stated that traffic congestion could decrease by approximately 40% by 2030 if planned transport concept measures are implemented. He noted the city's vehicle registration has surged to over 503,000, far exceeding its capacity. Aliyev suggested restrictions on vehicle entry or registration might be necessary in the future.

item.title: Russia May Have Shot Down Three of Its Own Military Helicopters
item.description: Russia may have mistakenly shot down three of its own military helicopters, possibly mistaking them for Ukrainian drones. Air defense units reportedly launched the helicopters to repel attacks on the Leningrad region. Various sources indicate that a total of seven crew members were killed in the incident.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Presidential Election: Digital Signatures and Primaries
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential election process is underway, with 11 candidates, including incumbent Sadyr Japarov. A notable feature is the use of digital technology, specifically the "Tunduk" app, for collecting required signatures. This digital approach presents both opportunities and challenges for candidates and voters.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Relocating Major Universities to New Cities
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Science and Higher Education is evaluating plans to move major universities from Almaty to either Korday or the new city of Qonaev. The decision hinges on which city can develop the necessary infrastructure, including utilities and heating, first. Several universities have expressed readiness to relocate.

item.title: Taliban Invite Russian Companies to Invest in Afghan Mineral Extraction
item.description: Taliban authorities have invited Russian companies to partner with Afghan firms for mineral extraction, proposing joint investments in mining and infrastructure projects. Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Overchuk led a delegation for talks in Kabul, aiming to rebuild Afghanistan's economy, create jobs, and expand bilateral trade.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans 15 MW Floating Solar Power Plant at HPP-5
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to build a 15 MW floating solar power plant at HPP-5 in the Chuy region, a project by Open Joint Stock Company "Chakan HPP" in cooperation with the Asian Development Bank. A pilot 0.1 MW floating solar power station is already operational at the site. The bank estimates the potential for additional floating solar stations in Kyrgyzstan at 176 MW.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Pilot New Social Benefit Rules Focusing on Family Income
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection will launch a pilot project on January 11, 2027, to revise social benefit payment rules. The project will cover 12 out of 36 types of social payments, targeting families deemed high-income or affluent. The ministry aims to better account for families' actual financial situations, as current rules may not always reflect their material well-being, leading to unequal distribution of aid.

item.title: Heads of Kazakhstan's Sovereign Wealth Fund and National Railway Detained for Corruption
item.description: The chairman of Kazakhstan's state fund "Samruk-Kazyna," Nurlan Zhakupov, and the head of the national railway company KTZ, Yelsas Otynshiev, have been detained on suspicion of corruption. The detentions were carried out by the National Security Committee's anti-corruption service on November 11. The committee has not specified the exact charges or the amounts involved in the case.

item.title: Kazakhstan Science Funding Audit Reveals Most Projects Missed Sales Targets
item.description: An audit by Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber found that 103 out of 141 publicly funded science projects failed to meet sales targets over the past three years, representing a loss of 22 billion tenge (approx. $49 million). The chamber's chairman noted that research institutions often cite publications and patents as success indicators, but auditors found no record of agreements for 60 examined patents.
